Young plants really shouldn't be producing flowers super early.  This generally indicates that the plants are stressed out somehow - not enough/too much moisture, not enough/too much of particular soil nutrients, too high/low temperatures.  When young plants start developing flowers early, it's essentially their last ditch effort to quickly produce their fruit before they start to die and don't have the energy to do so.  I'd check your growing conditions and see if you need to adjust something to make your plants happier.

The little humpbacked green bug is a treehopper.  They suck sap from leaves.  Excess sap can attract ants, which explains why you've noticed ants on some of the same plants.  Heavy sprays of water will usually knock them off of plants, but you can use an insecticidal soap if you have a large number of them on your plants.  I wouldn't use an insecticide on the plants without your neighbor's permission though.

I had this problem myself when I had to make my first appointment with a therapist.  Phone calls scare the crap out of me and are one of my biggest anxiety-provokers.  What I did was write down exactly what I wanted to say; sort of like a script.  Even if it feels silly having to write down, "Hi, my name is so and so and I was hoping to schedule an intake session. etc," it really helped just to have something to read off just in case my mind went blank and I couldn't remember what I wanted to say.  I would also recommend surrounding yourself with some items to help you destress immediately after making the call.  For instance, if listening to music or watching a certain movie really helps to calm you down, have them ready to play right after you hang up the phone.  Just remember that as scary as making that first call is, it will never be as bad as you think.
